<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.

Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

When loading a model from S3 (e.g., via `runai_streamer`) without specifying `--served-model-name`, the default served model name inherits the URI containing a colon (:), such as `s3://xxx.` During engine warmup, the parser mistakenly interprets the colon as a delimiter for a LoRA adapter (<lora_name>:<lora_path>). As a result, the engine crashes because the LoRA adapter cannot be found.

## Modifications

Refactor `_parse_model_parameter` to properly distinguish between URI schemes (e.g., s3://) and LoRA specifications, preventing false-positive LoRA resolution.

files.patch:
@@ -40,17 +40,24 @@ def __init__(self, tokenizer_manager: TokenizerManager):
     def _parse_model_parameter(self, model: str) -> Tuple[str, Optional[str]]:
         """Parse 'base-model:adapter-name' syntax to extract LoRA adapter.
 
-        Returns (base_model, adapter_name) or (model, None) if no colon present.
+        Returns (base_model, adapter_name), preserving an exact served model
+        name even when it contains colons (e.g. an object-storage URI).
         """
         if ":" not in model:
             return model, None
 
-        # Split on first colon only to handle model paths with multiple colons
-        parts = model.split(":", 1)
-        base_model = parts[0].strip()
-        adapter_name = parts[1].strip() or None
+        served_model_name = self.tokenizer_manager.served_model_name
+        if model == served_model_name:
+            return model, None
+
+        # Match the full served name before splitting URI schemes like s3://.
+        if model.startswith(f"{served_model_name}:"):
+            base_model = served_model_name
+            adapter_name = model[len(served_model_name) + 1 :]
+        else:
+            base_model, adapter_name = model.split(":", 1)
 
-        return base_model, adapter_name
+        return base_model.strip(), adapter_name.strip() or None
